title: Gluing quasi-affine principal neighbourhoods of a quasi-compact subset
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $E\subseteq |Y|$ a quasi-compact subset with its subspace topology (every cover by relative open subsets has a finite subcover). An open subscheme is understood as in [def-weil-open-immersion]. A scheme is quasi-affine if it is isomorphic to a quasi-compact open subscheme of an affine scheme [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For an open subscheme $V\subseteq Y$ and $g\in\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$ put $V_g=\{v\in V:g_v\in\mathcal O_{V,v}^{\times}\}$. The following are equivalent: (i) there exists a quasi-compact quasi-affine open subscheme $U\subseteq Y$ with $E\subseteq |U|$; (ii) for every $e\in E$ there exist an open subscheme $V_e\subseteq Y$ containing all of $E$, with $V_e$ quasi-separated (intersections of affine opens are quasi-compact), and $g_e\in\Gamma(V_e,\mathcal O_{V_e})$ such that $(V_e)_{g_e}$ is quasi-affine and contains $e$. The empty subset is allowed. No quasi-separatedness assumption is made on all of $Y$.

source.place: Lemma 3.7 (internally referenced as 3.6 after the numbering shift), printed p.14, equivalence (i)–(ii); preceding Lemma 3.6 gives the quasi-affine basic-open covering criterion. Online primary scan read; local archive WANTED.

proof.text: If $E=\varnothing$, take $U=\varnothing$, the affine spectrum of the zero ring; (ii) is vacuous. Otherwise, (i) implies (ii) by taking $V_e=U$ and $g_e=1$ for every $e\in E$: quasi-affine schemes are quasi-separated by [lem-trf-quasi-affine-canonical-affine-embedding], and $U_1=U$.

source.place: Raynaud, Lemma 3.7, printed p.14, with Lemma 3.6 for the final fixed-scheme criterion; primary scan read online, local archive WANTED.

proof.text: Assume (ii) and $E\ne\varnothing$. The relative opens $E\cap(V_e)_{g_e}$ cover $E$. Choose a finite subcover with indices $1,\ldots,n$, where $n\ge1$, and put $V=\bigcap_{i=1}^nV_i$. This is an open neighbourhood of all of $E$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], choose affine opens inside $V$ covering $E$; choose finitely many using quasi-compactness of $E$. Their union $W$ contains $E$, lies in $V$, and is quasi-compact since each affine is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs].

source.place: Raynaud, Lemma 3.7, printed p.14, with Lemma 3.6 for the final fixed-scheme criterion; primary scan read online, local archive WANTED.

proof.text: Write $f_i=g_i|_W$ and $B_i=W_{f_i}=W\cap(V_i)_{g_i}$; equality follows because restriction to an open does not change germs. The opens $B_i$ cover $E$. Choose a finite affine open cover $W=\bigcup_{j=1}^m A_j$ by [lem-pqf-finite-affine-cover-qc-open]. For each $i,j$, $B_i\cap A_j=(A_j)_{f_i|_{A_j}}$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime], hence quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Thus each $B_i$ is a finite union of quasi-compact subsets and is quasi-compact.

source.place: Raynaud, Lemma 3.7, printed p.14, with Lemma 3.6 for the final fixed-scheme criterion; primary scan read online, local archive WANTED.

proof.text: Each $B_i$ is an open subscheme of the quasi-affine scheme $(V_i)_{g_i}$. Compose its open embedding with an embedding of $(V_i)_{g_i}$ as an open subscheme of an affine scheme. The composite identifies $B_i$ with an open subscheme of that affine scheme; since $B_i$ is quasi-compact by the preceding step, it is quasi-affine by definition. Set $U=\bigcup_{i=1}^n B_i$. Then $E\subseteq U\subseteq W$, and $U$ is quasi-compact by finite union.

source.place: Raynaud, Lemma 3.7, printed p.14, with Lemma 3.6 for the final fixed-scheme criterion; primary scan read online, local archive WANTED.

proof.text: Every affine open of $U$ is also affine open in $V_1$, so any two intersect quasi-compactly by the assumed quasi-separatedness of $V_1$. Hence $U$ is quasi-separated in exactly the affine-intersection sense in the statement. Put $h_i=f_i|_U$. Since $B_i\subseteq U$, equality of germs gives $U_{h_i}=U\cap W_{f_i}=B_i$. These quasi-affine basic opens cover $U$. Apply [lem-sfb-qcqs-quasiaffine-basic-open-cover] to this qcqs scheme $U$ and the functions $h_i$ to obtain that $U$ is quasi-affine, proving (i).

source.place: Raynaud, Lemma 3.7, printed p.14, with Lemma 3.6 for the final fixed-scheme criterion; primary scan read online, local archive WANTED.

The item matches 3.7 hypothesis by hypothesis: V_e must contain all of E and be quasi-separated; Y is not assumed quasi-separated; empty E is allowed. Steps 1-5 check out. Step 1: empty E, and U itself with g=1. Step 2: finitely many (V_e)_{g_e} cover E, and W is a finite union of affines in the intersection of the V_i (affine-opens-basis and affine-qcqs leaves); this proves the quasi-compact neighbourhood W that Raynaud takes for granted. Step 4 (elementary): each B_i is quasi-affine and U is a finite union. Step 5: U is quasi-separated through V_1, U_{h_i}=B_i, and the new node applies. Edge cases checked: E empty, n=1, and the line with doubled origin with E the two origins (both sides false). New node lem-sfb-qcqs-quasiaffine-basic-open-cover is Raynaud 3.6.
